questions.question: What does the Liq Scalper wait for before it enters?
questions.answer: It watches liquidation events and configured market conditions, then may enter against a qualifying liquidation. It is not a general-purpose entry signal.

questions.question: How is the Optimized Liquidation bot different from the Liq Scalper?
questions.answer: The Optimized Liquidation bot derives reversion bands separately for each pair from that market’s recent behavior. The Liq Scalper uses its configured liquidation trigger and fair-value bands.

questions.question: Does the TV Signal bot choose the strategy, or does TradingView send the signal?
questions.answer: TradingView sends the webhook action; the TV Signal bot checks it and manages the resulting deal with Wick Hunter’s deal engine.

questions.question: Can the Manual Bot open a trade for me?
questions.answer: No. You open the position at the exchange; the Manual Bot may adopt eligible positions and manage them. It does not create the initial entry.

questions.question: Does the Hedge Bot choose which coin to trade?
questions.answer: No. The Hedge Bot attaches to an existing eligible position. It manages opposite-side hedge tranches according to its settings; it does not choose a pair or open the main position.

questions.question: Is DCA one of the five Wick Hunter bots?
questions.answer: No. DCA is an averaging ladder used to manage an open deal; it is not an entry bot or a sixth bot.

questions.question: Which bots can open the first position?
questions.answer: The entry bots include the Liq Scalper, Optimized Liquidation bot, and TV Signal bot. The Manual Bot adopts a position you opened, and the Hedge Bot attaches to an existing position.

questions.question: Do all bots use the same deal controls after an entry?
questions.answer: The guide describes a shared deal engine for DCA and exits, while each bot has its own eligibility and entry rules. Check the specific bot section for exceptions and supported controls.

questions.question: Are DCA levels measured from the original entry or from the latest average?
questions.answer: For the Liq Scalper’s static ladder, each level’s distance is measured from the deal’s original opening price and is not recalculated after earlier fills.

questions.question: Can a fast price move fill several DCA orders at once?
questions.answer: Yes. A DCA level fills as soon as price touches it; there is no bounce or cooldown requirement, so one fast candle can cross several levels.

questions.question: Does enabling a stop loss also cap the maximum DCA position size?
questions.answer: No. The stop loss is an exit control, not a sizing cap. The guide warns that total exposure must be calculated from the configured base order and DCA ladder.

questions.question: What does Volume scale change in the DCA ladder?
questions.answer: It multiplies the size of each successive DCA order. Review the generated ladder preview to see the amount at every level before saving.

questions.question: What does Step scale change in the DCA ladder?
questions.answer: It controls how the spacing between successive DCA levels grows. Use the ladder preview to check the resulting prices before enabling the strategy.

questions.question: What happens when I choose Scaled ATR for DCA distance?
questions.answer: The first DCA distance is derived from the pair’s recent ATR, then bounded by the configured minimum and maximum. The result is calculated when the deal opens and stays fixed for that deal.

questions.question: Will Scaled ATR fall back to Static DCA if candles are missing?
questions.answer: No. If required ATR history is missing, stale, or unsupported, the entry is refused with a reason; the bot does not silently use the static deviation instead.

questions.question: Why does a scaled ATR DCA entry show as refused?
questions.answer: The guide lists missing, stale, or unsupported required ATR history as refusal causes. Check the pair’s status and candle history, then verify the timeframe and length.

questions.question: When does the bot convert a percentage base order into dollars?
questions.answer: It resolves the wallet percentage once when a deal opens, then freezes that dollar amount for the life of the deal.

questions.question: Does the base order setting include the later DCA orders?
questions.answer: No. The base order controls the opening trade. The DCA ladder is configured separately and starts only after the base order fills.

questions.question: How does the Manual Bot anchor DCA levels when it adopts a position?
questions.answer: It calculates the ladder from the position’s average entry at pickup. It does not re-plan the ladder from the moving average after later fills.

questions.question: If I edit a running deal’s DCA, does that update the Manual Bot template?
questions.answer: No. Deal-level edits in Terminal belong to that deal. They do not change the bot’s saved configuration.

questions.question: Does the Liq Scalper take profit start enabled?
questions.answer: Yes. The take-profit control is on by default. Check the selected target type and value before starting the bot.

questions.question: Does the Liq Scalper stop loss start enabled?
questions.answer: No. Stop loss ships off. Until you enable and configure it, the stop-loss setting does not automatically close a losing deal.

questions.question: Will a real exchange stop order keep working if Wick Hunter goes offline?
questions.answer: When the venue can hold the stop, Wick Hunter places a reduce-only stop order on the exchange. Check the selected venue and the order’s reported status; support cannot promise an exact execution price.

questions.question: Does a fixed take-profit target move upward as the market rises?
questions.answer: No. A fixed target does not trail price. It is re-placed when the deal’s average changes after a DCA fill, but it does not follow market moves on its own.

questions.question: What makes a trailing take profit different from a fixed target?
questions.answer: A trailing take profit follows favorable price movement according to its configured activation and offset. A fixed target remains at its configured level, apart from re-anchoring when the average entry changes.

questions.question: What price does the paired target use to decide when to close?
questions.answer: It is a combined P&L target across the main position, open hedge tranches, realized hedge results, funding, and fees—not a single exchange price order. Wick Hunter watches that calculation and then attempts market closes for the open legs.

questions.question: Does hedge trailing arm a stop on an unprotected tranche?
questions.answer: No. Trailing only moves stops that are already armed. The activation and offset settings control how an armed stop follows price.

questions.question: Does a Hedge Bot hedge close my losing main position?
questions.answer: No. A hedge opens an opposite-side position and keeps the main deal open. It can offset part of the loss, but it is not a stop loss or a guaranteed recovery.

questions.question: Can a hedge lose money through fees and funding?
questions.answer: Yes. The hedge adds another position, so it brings its own margin, fees, and funding. A hedge that never banks gains can add cost.

questions.question: Why must the exchange account be in Hedge Mode before hedge tranches open?
questions.answer: Hedge Mode keeps a long and short position on the same symbol separate. In one-way mode, an opposite order may reduce or close the main position instead of creating a hedge.

questions.question: What does Max w/o stop limit: tranche count or position size?
questions.answer: It is a size budget for hedge exposure that has no stop, measured as a percentage of the main position. It is not a count of tranches.

questions.question: When does an unprotected hedge tranche stop counting against the budget?
questions.answer: It stops counting only after a stop is armed for that tranche. A tranche that is profitable but has not reached the activation threshold is still unprotected.

questions.question: Does the Hedge Bot ladder Size % mean the next order size?
questions.answer: No. Size % is the total hedge you want to be holding at that ladder level. Treating it as each new order size can create a much larger hedge than intended.

questions.question: What is included in the paired hedge take-profit calculation?
questions.answer: The combined target considers the main position, open hedge tranches, realized hedge results and funding as described in the guide. When reached, Wick Hunter attempts market closes for the main and remaining hedge legs; actual fills occur on the exchange.

questions.question: Why is my exchange P&L different from Wick Hunter’s P&L?
questions.answer: Exchanges publish different trade, fee, and funding details. Wick Hunter shows available venue data and leaves unknown information blank rather than guessing; check the exchange-specific notice.

questions.question: Are the P&L daily totals based on my local timezone?
questions.answer: No. P&L days use UTC, matching the Day P&L tile and the exchange day count.

questions.question: Is minute-by-minute Deal Replay available on the current P&L page?
questions.answer: No. Deal Replay is unavailable in this released app build; its Replay navigation and guide entry are hidden. The P&L page itself remains available.

questions.question: Which exchange supplies the candles used for a trading decision?
questions.answer: The exchange and product selected for the deal supply its candles. For example, spot and perpetual products can use different venue books.

questions.question: Why are the price numbers on the chart axis missing the order names?
questions.answer: Order names appear as tags beside the chart lines, while the right axis shows prices only. This keeps the price axis readable when many lines are present.

questions.question: Can I cancel a chart drag without sending a change?
questions.answer: Yes. Press Escape to abandon a staged drag; the line returns to the exchange-reported price and no server request is made.

questions.question: Why does editing an unfilled DCA cancel and replace the other resting DCAs?
questions.answer: The DCA prices are derived from the edited ladder, so the other resting levels must be cancelled and placed again to keep the ladder consistent. Review the staged order count before committing.

questions.question: Can I use the Terminal order ticket without turning on its separate switch?
questions.answer: No. The manual order ticket stays off until explicitly enabled. It is separate from bot activity and lets you choose order side, type, and size.

questions.question: Does the Liq Scalper buy every liquidation it sees?
questions.answer: No. It fades qualifying liquidation events only when its configured trigger and market filters permit an entry. It does not act on every print.

questions.question: What does Min liquidation size filter?
questions.answer: It sets the minimum USD value for a forced-liquidation print to count as a trigger. A print below the threshold is ignored.

questions.question: Does the liquidation size setting determine my order size?
questions.answer: No. It is an entry trigger threshold. The Base order controls the opening order size.

questions.question: What does VWMA mean in the Liq Scalper settings?
questions.answer: VWMA is a volume-weighted moving average. It forms a fair-value reference from recent candles, giving higher-volume candles more weight.

questions.question: What are the Liq Scalper bands measured against?
questions.answer: The entry bands are measured from the configured fair-value line. The liquidation feed supplies the triggering event; the bot evaluates it against its own market and price data.

questions.question: Can the Liq Scalper use a liquidation feed from one exchange and trade another?
questions.answer: The feed may trigger an event, but the bot uses the selected trading account’s own symbol and price book to make its decision. It does not trade using the other venue’s price.

questions.question: What are the Liq Scalper pair filters for?
questions.answer: They decide which pairs enter the bot’s watch set. The guide groups them under Volume, Funding, Volatility, and Market limits; only active rules filter the set.

questions.question: Is the Liq Scalper’s 24-hour volume filter based on midnight UTC?
questions.answer: No. It is a rolling 24-hour volume floor read from the exchange where the account trades, not a figure that resets at midnight UTC.

questions.question: How do I turn off the minimum rolling volume filter?
questions.answer: Leave it blank or set it to 0. The guide says 0 means the minimum volume rule is off.

questions.question: What currency does Minimum coin market cap use?
questions.answer: It is entered as a USD value. The field accepts documented shorthand and reads back the normalized amount before saving.

questions.question: Does Min leverage set the leverage on a new trade?
questions.answer: No. It filters pairs by the exchange’s maximum leverage support. It does not set the trade’s leverage.

questions.question: How does a volatility filter decide whether to exclude a pair?
questions.answer: Each row checks the last N closed candles on its timeframe. A pair is excluded if any individual candle moved more than the configured maximum percentage.

questions.question: What does Auto-refresh do to the Liq Scalper watch list?
questions.answer: It rebuilds the pair list at the configured interval by rerunning the filters. A pair can enter or leave the watch set when its market data changes.

questions.question: If I raise the liquidation trigger, will it increase the base order?
questions.answer: No. The trigger controls which liquidation events qualify; order size is set separately in Base order.

questions.question: When does the Liq Scalper place its DCA ladder?
questions.answer: The DCA ladder starts only after the base order has filled. Its levels then manage that open deal as price moves against it.

questions.question: Does the Summary panel limit my order size if it shows a warning?
questions.answer: No. The Summary panel is live arithmetic for review, not a setting or a hard limit. Use it to catch configuration risk before saving.

questions.question: Where can I see a complete Liq Scalper configuration example?
questions.answer: Open the Liq Scalper worked-example section. It walks through the bot’s settings and their resulting order behavior; treat its numbers as an example, not a recommendation.

questions.question: How does the Optimized Liquidation bot set entry bands for different pairs?
questions.answer: It derives its liquidation-reversion logic separately for each watched pair from that market’s recent behavior rather than using one fixed band for every pair.

questions.question: Are Optimized Liquidation bands shared across all pairs?
questions.answer: No. The bot calculates bands per pair from that pair’s history, so two markets can have different entry levels at the same time.

questions.question: What does the Optimized bot’s lookback period control?
questions.answer: It controls the historical window used to estimate the pair’s recent liquidation behavior. The guide shows the candle count and memory implications for the selected settings.

questions.question: Why can an Optimized Liquidation pair be unavailable during warm-up?
questions.answer: The bot needs enough valid history to calculate its per-pair bands. Until that history is ready, the pair remains in warm-up and is not treated as having a valid signal.

questions.question: Does the Optimized bot trade while its pair is warming up?
questions.answer: No. Warm-up means the required data is still being prepared; the pair must become ready before a signal can qualify for an entry.

questions.question: What does the Optimized bot do when a required data window is stale?
questions.answer: It marks the window stale or unavailable and retries the required data path. It does not pretend a missing or stale window is a valid signal.

questions.question: Do Optimized Liquidation pair filters use the trading exchange’s data?
questions.answer: The pair filters are based on the selected venue and its validated data for the account. Check the filter panel and Activity for the reason a pair is excluded.

questions.question: Does the Optimized bot’s liquidation threshold control its order size?
questions.answer: No. The threshold decides which events can qualify as entries. Base order and the deal settings control size and position management.

questions.question: Does Optimized Liquidation use the shared take-profit and stop-loss controls?
questions.answer: Yes. It hands accepted entries to the shared deal engine, whose exit settings manage the open position. Check the bot’s Exits section for its supported choices.

questions.question: Where can I see an end-to-end Optimized Liquidation example?
questions.answer: Use the worked example in the Optimized Liquidation guide. It shows how the pair-specific logic and shared deal settings fit together; its sample numbers are not a trading recommendation.

questions.question: Does TradingView need to reach my server from the public internet?
questions.answer: Yes. TradingView must be able to reach the bot’s public HTTPS webhook address. A local or private-network address cannot receive its alert.

questions.question: Do I need a paid TradingView plan for webhooks?
questions.answer: The setup guide says TradingView webhook notifications require a paid TradingView plan. Check TradingView’s current plan rules before configuring alerts.

questions.question: Why is my TradingView webhook URL unreachable from their alert service?
questions.answer: The server address must be publicly reachable over HTTPS with a valid certificate. A local address, home-network address, unusual port, or invalid certificate can prevent delivery.

questions.question: Can I copy the TV Signal URL while browsing Wick Hunter through localhost?
questions.answer: No. The webhook address is based on how you are browsing, so a locally copied address may be local too. Copy it from the public HTTPS dashboard address and preserve the bot path.

questions.question: Why does {{ticker}} open the wrong TradingView pair?
questions.answer: The placeholder can send the symbol for the chart where the alert was created, which may not match the exchange symbol. Use the exact pair name the bot expects or verify the emitted symbol in Recent signals.

questions.question: What must every TradingView message include?
questions.answer: Every accepted message needs the bot secret and an action. Most actions also need a symbol; the documented exceptions include close-everything, pause, and resume.

questions.question: Can I add a sentence before the JSON in my TradingView alert?
questions.answer: No. The message must match one of the documented formats. Extra text, smart quotes, or punctuation can make the payload malformed and cause refusal.

questions.question: Does renaming a TV Signal bot change its webhook URL?
questions.answer: No. The webhook URL is fixed for that bot’s life and renaming it does not change the address.

questions.question: Why should I treat the TradingView webhook URL like a password?
questions.answer: Anyone with the bot URL and secret can send actions to that bot without signing in. Keep both private and rotate the secret if either is exposed.

questions.question: What should I do if I posted my TradingView webhook secret publicly?
questions.answer: Treat the secret as compromised. Rotate it in the bot settings, replace it in your TradingView alert, and do not share the new secret in a support message.

questions.question: Can the TradingView alert override my saved base order size?
questions.answer: Yes. If the alert message carries its own size, that size overrides the bot’s Base order for that deal. Check the exact payload and configured size before sending live alerts.

questions.question: Does pressing Save on the TV Signal form leave a paused bot paused?
questions.answer: The troubleshooting guide says saving resumes the bot. Check the bot’s status after saving if you meant only to update its settings.

questions.question: The alert is in Recent signals but the bot did not enter. Where is the refusal reason?
questions.answer: Open the TV Signal form and read the Recent signals row. If the alert arrived, the app records whether it was refused and gives the reason there.

questions.question: What does “held by another bot” mean for a TradingView signal?
questions.answer: A pair has one manager at a time. If another bot already owns the pair, the TV Signal bot refuses the entry; close that deal or use another eligible pair.

questions.question: Why did a TradingView signal for my pair get rejected as a duplicate?
questions.answer: The same direction and symbol may have opened within the bot’s cooldown period. This is expected duplicate protection; lower the cooldown only if your strategy truly needs faster re-entry.

questions.question: Does a signal sent while the TV Signal bot is paused get replayed after I resume?
questions.answer: No. A paused bot refuses signals while paused; it does not queue them for later. Resume it before sending new alerts.

questions.question: What types of positions can the Manual Bot manage?
questions.answer: It adopts eligible open positions on a supported futures market and manages them with the configured DCA and exits. It does not create the initial position.

questions.question: How quickly does the Manual Bot usually adopt a position?
questions.answer: The guide says adoption is normally detected in about a second, using the exchange’s private position event, with recovery checks if that event is missed.

questions.question: Why would the Manual Bot ignore a position on a different market?
questions.answer: Each bot belongs to the market where it was created. A Manual Bot set up for USDT does not adopt a USDC position; create one on that market if supported.

questions.question: Can the Manual Bot adopt a position another Wick Hunter bot already owns?
questions.answer: No. One bot owns a pair at a time. The Manual Bot leaves a position alone if another app bot already manages that pair.

questions.question: Will the Manual Bot adopt the hedge leg created by Hedge Bot?
questions.answer: No. A hedge leg belongs to the Hedge Bot and is not adopted by the Manual Bot. The main position can still be managed by its owning bot.

questions.question: Does pausing Manual Bot close positions it already manages?
questions.answer: No. Pausing stops it from adopting new positions; positions it already manages continue to be managed through their configured exits.

questions.question: If Manual Bot is paused, will it manage a new position I open by hand?
questions.answer: No. A new position opened while it is paused is not adopted and receives no Manual Bot DCA, take profit, or stop loss.

questions.question: Where does the Manual Bot place its take-profit order?
questions.answer: Its take profit is a reduce-only limit order on the exchange. The stop-loss behavior is different and is managed by the app, so review the server-availability risk in the guide.

questions.question: Will the Manual Bot stop loss remain active if the Wick Hunter server goes down?
questions.answer: The Manual Bot’s stop loss is app-managed rather than an exchange-held order. If the app is offline it cannot monitor and execute that stop; check the exchange-held take profit separately.

questions.question: Do Manual Bot scope changes require a restart?
questions.answer: The direction and pair scope changes apply immediately to the next adoption check. Changes to DCA and exit settings govern positions picked up afterward.

questions.question: Where can I see why a position was skipped by Manual Bot?
questions.answer: Check Activity for scope exclusions and the server log for position ownership or safety exclusions. The guide lists the reason text to look for.

questions.question: Does enabling auto-attach open a hedge immediately?
questions.answer: No. Auto-attach makes the Hedge Bot watch eligible existing positions. A hedge tranche opens only after its configured adverse-move level is reached and all checks pass.

questions.question: Can more than one Hedge Bot be configured?
questions.answer: Yes. The guide supports multiple Hedge Bots, each with its own settings and pair scope. Confirm which bot is selected before editing its configuration.

questions.question: Are Hedge Bot settings saved as I type them?
questions.answer: No. Editing a field marks the form unsaved. Use Save hedge settings and read the status line to confirm whether the save succeeded.

questions.question: What does Split by main side change in Hedge settings?
questions.answer: It creates separate parameter columns for a long main position and a short main position. One config uses the same parameter set for both directions.

questions.question: From what price is each Hedge Bot ladder distance measured?
questions.answer: From the position’s current blended average entry, not the original entry. It re-anchors after each DCA fill, manual add, or partial close.

questions.question: Why can the hedge ladder skip a level even after price reaches it?
questions.answer: A new tranche can be blocked if it would exceed the global or per-level unstopped size budget, if the minimum tranche is not met, or if the exchange/account mode check fails. Read the active hedge panel and Activity reason.

questions.question: Does the paired take profit close every hedge tranche at once?
questions.answer: When the combined paired target is reached, Wick Hunter attempts market closes for the main position and remaining open hedge legs; actual fills occur on the exchange.

questions.question: Does trailing move the stop on the main position too?
questions.answer: No. The Hedge Bot’s trailing setting applies to armed hedge tranche stops. It does not trail the main position’s stop.

questions.question: What happens when I click Moderate, Slow, or Aggressive?
questions.answer: A template fills the Hedge Bot form with a complete starting configuration. Review all resulting values and save the settings before relying on them.

questions.question: Can I change hedge settings for only one pair?
questions.answer: Yes. The guide describes per-pair overrides for selected hedge settings. Save the override and verify it in the active hedge panel for that symbol.

questions.question: Can Hedge Bot run on spot markets?
questions.answer: No. The guide limits it to USDT perpetual futures, where the exchange can hold long and short positions on the same symbol.

questions.question: Has every supported hedge venue been tested with live orders?
questions.answer: No. The venue notes distinguish code coverage from live-account verification. Read the current venue note and start with the smallest permitted size when testing a newly verified market.

questions.question: Where can I see the Hedge Bot’s live status for one position?
questions.answer: Open Deals → View hedge for that deal. The active hedge panel shows the selected position, hedge state, relevant settings, and chart context.

questions.question: How do I expand the hedge chart on a small screen?
questions.answer: From Deals → View hedge, choose Expand to fill the app window. Restore or press Escape to return to the pair panel.

questions.question: Do DCA levels require price to bounce before they fill?
questions.answer: No. A level fills when price touches it; no bounce is required. A fast move can fill multiple levels before price reverses.

questions.question: Does the DCA ladder use a cooldown between fills?
questions.answer: No. The guide states there is no minimum time between level fills. Do not assume the ladder will pause between levels during a fast move.

questions.question: If I set volume scale to 1, how does order size change?
questions.answer: A volume scale of 1 keeps each successive DCA order the same size. The ladder preview shows each order amount before you save.

questions.question: If I set step scale to 1, how do the DCA distances grow?
questions.answer: A step scale of 1 makes the levels evenly spaced. Check the preview for the resulting prices and spacing.

questions.question: What happens if I set Scaled ATR maximum deviation to zero?
questions.answer: Zero means no maximum ceiling in the documented Scaled ATR setting. On a very volatile pair, the first DCA can be placed far away; review the preview before saving.

questions.question: Why does the form refuse a maximum ATR deviation below the minimum?
questions.answer: That combination is invalid, so saving is refused. Raise the maximum to at least the minimum or lower the minimum, then review the preview again.

questions.question: Does the ATR DCA timeframe have to match the VWMA timeframe?
questions.answer: No. The guide says ATR uses its own timeframe and length; it can use a different interval from the VWMA signal settings.

questions.question: Can I drag a DCA that has already filled?
questions.answer: No. A filled DCA has no handle because it represents an order that already executed. Only unfilled DCA levels can be moved.

questions.question: What happens to a bot’s DCA following after I edit levels in Terminal?
questions.answer: The edited deal stops following the bot’s DCA settings. Its committed values remain specific to that deal, including after a restart.

questions.question: If an exchange refuses my edited price, does Terminal leave the chart at that price?
questions.answer: No. The line returns to the price actually resting at the exchange, and the venue’s refusal reason appears in the action line.

questions.question: Why does the staged bar count cancels and replacement orders?
questions.answer: The exchange cannot edit those resting orders in place. Wick Hunter must confirm cancellation before placing replacements, so the staged bar previews the order operations before commit.

questions.question: Does the P&L page use UTC for every day in the table?
questions.answer: Yes. Each P&L day uses UTC and matches the header’s Day P&L tile and the exchange’s day count.

questions.question: Why is an exchange fee missing from a closed-trade calculation?
questions.answer: The venue may not provide enough information to tie that fee to a trade. Wick Hunter shows less rather than assigning an unverified fee to the wrong trade.

questions.question: What does the USDT/USD switch change on the P&L page?
questions.answer: It changes the selected currency basis for the displayed equity and wallet values. It does not change the exchange’s recorded orders or fills.

questions.question: How long does TV Signal remember a completed idempotency key?
questions.answer: Completed IDs are remembered for seven days across restarts. Reuse the key only when retrying that same command; each new alert firing needs its own unique key.

questions.question: How far back can Wick Hunter import WEEX fills?
questions.answer: The guide says WEEX permits up to 365 days of fills. The history note shows how far the import has progressed; reaching the available window does not prove the account has no older history.

questions.question: Does tapping the Home chart show the nearest sample on mobile?
questions.answer: Yes. Hover or tap the line to read the nearest real sample’s value and time.

questions.question: Do spot and perpetual charts use the same exchange book?
questions.answer: No. A price decision uses the selected product’s book; the guide distinguishes Spot, linear perpetual, and inverse contract candles where applicable.

questions.question: What do the small labels beside Terminal chart lines mean?
questions.answer: They name the line, such as Avg Price or DCA 2. The numeric price remains on the right-hand axis so line names do not crowd the axis.

questions.question: Can I copy the worked-example settings and expect the same trades?
questions.answer: No. The example demonstrates how the settings combine; it is not a promise of results or a recommendation. Confirm each setting against your own limits before enabling a bot.

questions.question: Are the worked-example bot sizes a recommended trade amount?
questions.answer: No. The worked example explains the fields and resulting arithmetic. Choose sizing based on your own risk limits; support cannot recommend a trade size.

questions.question: Does the Hedge Bot worked example prove the hedge will recover a loss?
questions.answer: No. It illustrates how the hedge ladder and paired target behave with sample values. It does not guarantee recovery or profit.

questions.question: Does changing the bot name affect its trading decisions?
questions.answer: No. The name labels the bot on My Bots and in Activity; it has no effect on its trading decisions.

questions.question: Where do I choose which direction the Liq Scalper may trade?
questions.answer: Open the bot’s Main settings and set its allowed side. The direction setting limits which side of a qualifying liquidation the bot may take.

questions.question: Will a pair removed by filters stay excluded until I edit the bot?
questions.answer: Not necessarily. Auto-refresh rebuilds the watch set, so a pair can enter or leave as its current exchange data and filter results change.

questions.question: What happens if I leave minimum rolling volume blank?
questions.answer: Blank or zero turns the minimum rolling-volume rule off. The setting ships off unless you configure a floor.

questions.question: Does the volatility filter average candle moves together?
questions.answer: No. It checks each of the last N closed candles individually and excludes a pair if any single candle exceeds the configured maximum move.

questions.question: Does a higher-volume candle affect the VWMA more than a quiet candle?
questions.answer: Yes. VWMA weights each candle’s close by its volume, so a candle with more traded volume has more influence on the fair-value line.

questions.question: Can the Liq Scalper Summary panel stop an unsafe configuration from trading?
questions.answer: The panel is a preview, not a limit. It displays arithmetic to help you spot risk; the configuration still depends on the settings you save.

questions.question: When is an ATR take-profit distance calculated for a deal?
questions.answer: The ATR-based distance is calculated once when the deal opens and stays fixed for that deal’s life. If ATR cannot be computed, the entry is refused rather than silently switching to another target mode.

questions.question: Can the Optimized bot watch only selected pairs?
questions.answer: Yes. Set the watched pair scope in its Main settings. The bot evaluates its logic separately for each pair in that watch set.

questions.question: What should I check if an Optimized pair stays in warm-up?
questions.answer: Check whether the required history window is available and current. The pair cannot produce its normal entry signal until the required data is ready.

questions.question: Does the Optimized bot silently use old data when a history request fails?
questions.answer: No. The guide keeps incomplete or stale windows visible and retries them; it does not treat an unavailable window as a current valid signal.

questions.question: Where are the Optimized bot’s take-profit and stop-loss settings?
questions.answer: Open its Exits section. It uses the shared deal exit engine, and the section lists the supported take-profit and stop-loss choices.

questions.question: Can a TV Signal alert open a short if the bot is long-only?
questions.answer: No. Direction is checked before an order is placed. A signal outside the bot’s allowed side is refused and shown in Recent signals.

questions.question: Can I reuse one TV Signal webhook URL for a different bot?
questions.answer: Use the URL and secret shown for the specific bot. Each address belongs to that bot; a message sent to another bot’s URL does not get redirected.

questions.question: Does every TV Signal action need a symbol?
questions.answer: Most actions need a symbol. The documented exceptions are close everything, pause, and resume.

questions.question: When is a percentage-based TV Signal order size frozen?
questions.answer: The wallet percentage is resolved when the deal opens and then remains fixed for that deal’s lifetime.

questions.question: Can two bots manage the same pair at the same time?
questions.answer: No. The product uses one manager per pair at a time. A signal that targets a pair already owned by another bot is refused.

questions.question: Will the Manual Bot manage a position created by another Wick Hunter bot?
questions.answer: No. If an app bot’s order records own the pair, the Manual Bot stands aside rather than adopting it.

questions.question: When I pause the Manual Bot, what stops immediately?
questions.answer: Pausing stops new position adoption. It does not abandon positions already managed, which continue through their configured exits.

questions.question: Do I need to restart the Manual Bot after changing its direction filter?
questions.answer: No. Direction and pair scope apply immediately to the next adoption check after saving.

questions.question: Does the Manual Bot’s stop loss live at the exchange?
questions.answer: No. Its stop loss is monitored by the app, while its take profit is a reduce-only order on the exchange. The distinction matters if the server is offline.

questions.question: Why does Manual Bot skip a pair with an unresolved order?
questions.answer: An unfinished or unconfirmed order can hold ownership of that pair. The bot blocks adoption rather than guessing whether the order opened a position.

questions.question: Will Manual Bot adopt a spot wallet balance?
questions.answer: No. It manages eligible derivatives positions, not a spot balance or a dated future outside its supported market.

questions.question: Does the Hedge Bot create a main position before it attaches?
questions.answer: No. It only adopts positions that already exist; its job is to add opposite-side hedge tranches after configured levels are reached.

questions.question: What does Minimum DCA to Hedge prevent?
questions.answer: It can prevent a hedge from opening before a selected deal bot reaches the configured minimum DCA count. The option starts off and can be configured per bot.

questions.question: How can I tell whether Hedge Bot settings were saved?
questions.answer: Read the status line next to Save hedge settings. It reports whether there are unsaved edits or whether the save completed.

questions.question: Can a hedge tranche open for less than the ladder requested?
questions.answer: Yes. The guide says a tranche may be smaller than requested or may not open if size budgets or other checks prevent it.

questions.question: Does a profitable hedge count as protected before its stop arms?
questions.answer: No. It remains unprotected until the stop is armed, even if its current P&L is positive.

questions.question: Does Max w/o stop count how many hedge tranches are open?
questions.answer: No. It is a size budget for unprotected hedge exposure, measured against the main position, not a tranche count.

questions.question: Does the Hedge Bot select LONG MAIN or SHORT MAIN settings again after a DCA changes the average?
questions.answer: No. It chooses the settings column when it attaches, based on the main position’s direction, and keeps that choice for the attachment. The ladder distances themselves re-anchor to the changing average.

questions.question: What does the hedge trail offset measure?
questions.answer: It controls how far the armed hedge stop trails behind price as the tranche earns. It changes the stop behavior, not the main position’s exit.

questions.question: Does selecting a Hedge Bot template save it automatically?
questions.answer: No. The template fills the form with a starting configuration; review the values and use Save hedge settings to apply them.

questions.question: Do hedge per-pair overrides apply as soon as I type them?
questions.answer: No. Save the override. The guide says the supported pair-specific values take effect once saved.

questions.question: Why does View hedge open with a pair already selected?
questions.answer: It opens the Active hedge panel for that deal’s pair so you can inspect its current hedge state and chart context.

questions.question: Can I use the Hedge Bot on inverse or spot markets?
questions.answer: No. The guide limits Hedge Bot to USDT perpetual futures. Its position-mode and order support depend on the selected venue.

questions.question: Does the static DCA ladder move when the market average entry changes?
questions.answer: No. Static levels stay measured from the deal’s original opening price, even after fills change the average entry.

questions.question: Why is a DCA ladder described as static?
questions.answer: Its level prices are set from the original deal entry and do not move when earlier DCAs change the position average.

questions.question: Can I preview every generated DCA order size before saving?
questions.answer: Yes. The DCA scale panel shows the generated ladder so you can inspect the size at each level before you save.

questions.question: Why is a minimum deviation useful with Scaled ATR?
questions.answer: A minimum deviation prevents the first DCA from being placed too close on a quiet pair, where ordinary price noise could fill it prematurely.

questions.question: What is the risk of leaving the Scaled ATR maximum deviation at zero?
questions.answer: With no ceiling, ATR on a very volatile pair can place the first level far away so that it never fills. Review the preview and choose bounds intentionally.

questions.question: Can Scaled ATR use the same history settings as the VWMA?
questions.answer: It has its own timeframe and length settings. Those control ladder sizing; VWMA timeframe settings control entry timing.

questions.question: Does Scaled ATR recalculate DCA levels as volatility changes after entry?
questions.answer: No. It calculates the ladder when the deal opens, then freezes those levels for that deal.

questions.question: What happens if the wallet balance cannot resolve a percentage order size?
questions.answer: The bot cannot safely calculate the requested dollar amount. Check the connected account’s balance and the refusal reason before retrying.

questions.question: Is the Base order the total maximum exposure for the whole deal?
questions.answer: No. It sizes the opening order only. Add the configured DCA amounts when calculating possible total exposure.

questions.question: If Volume scale is 2, how do successive DCA sizes change?
questions.answer: Each successive DCA order doubles from the previous size. Use the preview to see the full resulting ladder, because later levels grow quickly.

questions.question: What is the Manual Bot DCA anchor price?
questions.answer: It is the adopted position’s average entry at pickup. The bot plans the ladder once from that anchor rather than re-planning it later.

questions.question: Does Manual Bot size its first DCA from the bot’s entry order?
questions.answer: It has no entry order of its own. Its DCA ladder is configured for the existing position it adopts and is calculated from that position at pickup.

questions.question: What does “Fixed %” take profit do after the position average changes?
questions.answer: It cancels and re-places its reduce-only target from the new average after a DCA fill. It does not trail the target upward with market price.

questions.question: Does the Liq Scalper support a trailing take-profit target?
questions.answer: The guide lists Fixed %, Trailing, and ATR take-profit sources for the Liq Scalper’s single-target mode. Check the form for the currently available choices.

questions.question: When does the trailing take profit begin to follow price?
questions.answer: It begins after its configured activation condition is met, then follows the favorable move by the configured offset. Check the guide’s field definitions before choosing values.

questions.question: What does the stop-loss offset change?
questions.answer: The offset determines where the stop is placed relative to the selected reference. Its meaning depends on the offset mode, so read the field description before saving a percentage.

questions.question: Can a configured stop loss prevent liquidation in every market condition?
questions.answer: No. A stop is an exit instruction, not a guarantee of execution price or protection from all exchange or market failures. Keep the position size within your risk limits.

questions.question: Does pausing a bot cancel an exchange-held stop order?
questions.answer: A real stop order belongs to the position and is separate from whether a bot accepts new entries. Check the deal and venue order status before assuming protection changed.

questions.question: Why does the chart label the paired TP as a projected target?
questions.answer: It is a combined target monitored by Wick Hunter, not an exchange order resting at that price. When reached, Wick Hunter attempts market closes for both legs; actual fills occur on the exchange.

questions.question: Does the paired hedge exit include funding?
questions.answer: The paired target calculation includes the funding and realized hedge results described by the guide, alongside the position P&L. It is one combined exit for the pair.

questions.question: Why is Aster closed P&L a little different from my wallet change?
questions.answer: Aster does not expose a closed-position endpoint, so Wick Hunter rebuilds P&L from the account ledger. Some entry fees cannot be tied to one trade and are left out rather than guessed.

questions.question: Does Wick Hunter use the local calendar date for daily P&L?
questions.answer: No. P&L days are based on UTC, matching the daily tile and exchange count.

questions.question: Why might a missing exchange field show as blank instead of zero?
questions.answer: The P&L view does not invent fields the venue did not publish. A blank indicates the app cannot verify that value from the exchange data.

questions.question: What is the difference between Manual Bot saying “picked up” and “now managing”?
questions.answer: “Picked up” means the bot took responsibility and is attempting protection. “Now managing” confirms the venue accepted and the app read back the take-profit and DCA orders; if protection does not arrive, look for an UNPROTECTED alert.

questions.question: Does the WEEX history import restart from zero after an app restart?
questions.answer: No. The import saves its progress across restarts and retries unavailable reads, so it can continue from its saved position.

questions.question: Can Terminal show more than one deal at a time?
questions.answer: The Terminal view is focused on one open deal at a time. Select the deal you want to inspect from the app’s deal controls.

questions.question: What does the Avg Price line represent on the Terminal chart?
questions.answer: It shows the position’s blended average entry. It is not an order, so it has no drag handle.

questions.question: Can I move a DCA line using a touchscreen?
questions.answer: Yes. Unfilled DCA lines can be moved with a mouse, finger, or arrow keys. The change is staged until you choose Review & commit.

questions.question: What does a red order-line handle mean while I am dragging?
questions.answer: The staged price is currently invalid for that order, such as being on the wrong side of entry or out of DCA order. Read the warning beside the line and adjust it before committing.

questions.question: Can I drag the average-price line?
questions.answer: No. Avg Price describes the position’s cost; it is not an order, so it has no handle.

questions.question: What happens if I make a second change before the first commit finishes?
questions.answer: The second change wins for that order; the older reply is discarded so it cannot overwrite the newer choice.

questions.question: Can I open a Terminal-ticket position and have a bot manage it?
questions.answer: Yes. Choose a bot under Managed by; the new position is assigned to that bot and uses its TP, stop, and DCA settings. You can instead give this position its own settings without creating a bot.

questions.question: Why is my Bybit spot candle different from the Bybit perpetual candle?
questions.answer: They come from different product books. Wick Hunter uses the Spot book for Spot and the relevant linear or inverse book for perpetual contracts.

questions.question: What happens if I change the Liq Scalper name?
questions.answer: Only the label shown on My Bots and Activity changes. The name does not affect any trading decision.

questions.question: Can I let the Liq Scalper open both long and short deals?
questions.answer: Yes, if Direction is set to Both and the selected market supports those sides. Direction limits which side it may take.

questions.question: What does the Liq Scalper max-deals setting limit?
questions.answer: It limits the number of open deals the bot may hold at once. It is separate from pair filters and order sizing.

questions.question: If a pair filter group is collapsed, is the filter switched off?
questions.answer: No. Collapsing a group only changes the form display; it does not disable a saved rule.

questions.question: How can I tell whether my Liq Scalper pair filters are incomplete?
questions.answer: The Pairs summary shows counts for active and incomplete rules. Open the relevant group to see the field help and correct incomplete settings.

questions.question: Does a blank optional pair-filter value exclude all coins?
questions.answer: No. For fields documented as blank or zero = off, an empty value leaves that rule inactive. Check the field’s own help before relying on that default.

questions.question: Why did a pair disappear from the Liq Scalper watch list?
questions.answer: The watch list is rebuilt from the active pair filters. Check the pair’s volume, funding, volatility, market-limit results, and latest refresh status.

questions.question: Do category exclusions affect just the next refresh or all future refreshes?
questions.answer: They are saved filters used whenever the watch list is rebuilt. Review the exclusions and auto-refresh interval in Pairs.

questions.question: Does the volatility setting inspect live candles or closed candles?
questions.answer: It evaluates each of the last N closed candles for the configured timeframe.

questions.question: How many volatility timeframes can I configure?
questions.answer: The guide supports a list of timeframe rows, including 4h and 1d. Each row has its own maximum move and lookback count.

questions.question: Why is a volatility window marked missing or stale?
questions.answer: The required Hub snapshot may be incomplete or stale. The app retries requested missing windows every five minutes until the exchange fills them.

questions.question: Should I restart the bot if it is waiting for volatility data?
questions.answer: First check Activity and the bot card for warm-up or recovery status. The app retries missing requested windows; keep the Hub updated and allow the retry interval before escalating.

questions.question: Is the volume floor measured in the exchange’s own market?
questions.answer: Yes. The rolling 24-hour volume rule is read from the exchange the bot trades on.

questions.question: Can I type 250M into the Liq Scalper market-cap filter?
questions.answer: Yes. The guide accepts shorthand such as 250M and normalizes it to a USD amount for review before saving.

questions.question: If a coin supports less leverage than my filter, can it still be selected?
questions.answer: No. The minimum-leverage rule requires the pair’s maximum leverage on that exchange to be at least the configured floor.

questions.question: Do liquidation bands determine the Liq Scalper order amount?
questions.answer: No. The signal fields decide when an entry can fire. The Base order field determines the opening order size.

questions.question: Does VWMA use the average price of the whole day?
questions.answer: No. Its value is calculated from its configured number of recent candles, with each candle’s close weighted by volume.

questions.question: Why does my percentage-based base order not change as my wallet changes later?
questions.answer: The wallet percentage is converted to a dollar amount once when the deal opens; that amount remains frozen for the deal.

questions.question: Does DCA start before the Liq Scalper base order fills?
questions.answer: No. The DCA ladder and exits begin only after the opening base order has actually filled on the exchange.

questions.question: Where can I preview the Liq Scalper’s generated DCA ladder?
questions.answer: Open the DCA scale section and review its generated ladder table before saving. It shows the sizes and resulting levels from your inputs.

questions.question: Can the Liq Scalper use ATR-based take profit?
questions.answer: The guide lists ATR as an available take-profit source in single-target mode, alongside Fixed % and Trailing. Check the current form for its required fields.

questions.question: Does Fixed % take profit re-place after a manual add to the deal?
questions.answer: The target is based on average entry and re-anchors after the average changes, including manual adds described by the shared deal engine.

questions.question: What does turning off stop loss mean for an open Liq Scalper deal?
questions.answer: It means the bot has no automatic stop-loss exit configured. DCA or an enabled Hedge Bot may still manage exposure, but neither should be assumed to cap the loss.

questions.question: Should I copy a Liq Scalper worked example directly to a live account?
questions.answer: Treat it as an explanation of the form and arithmetic, not a recommendation. Review the full ladder, exits, market rules, and potential exposure before any live use.

questions.question: Does the Optimized Liquidation bot have its own pair list?
questions.answer: Yes. It has a watched set for the pairs whose recent behavior it evaluates. Review its Main and pair-filter settings to see that scope.

questions.question: Why do two Optimized Liquidation pairs show different bands?
questions.answer: The bot builds the entry logic independently for each pair from that market’s own recent history, so their bands can differ.

questions.question: Why can a longer Optimized lookback need more memory?
questions.answer: The bot retains more candle history to estimate each pair’s behavior. The guide explains the memory cost of the selected lookback and timeframe.

questions.question: Can an Optimized pair trade before its history window is ready?
questions.answer: No. A pair needs its required history to produce valid bands; while it warms up, it does not have a ready signal.

questions.question: What does a history ceiling control for the Optimized bot?
questions.answer: It bounds how much historical data the bot can request for its lookback. Check the guide’s candle-count and memory examples before increasing it.

questions.question: Does the Optimized bot’s liquidation minimum filter the same way as its entry bands?
questions.answer: They are separate conditions: the event threshold filters liquidation prints, while the pair-specific bands determine whether price is stretched enough for an entry.

questions.question: Where can I check whether an Optimized pair is still warming up?
questions.answer: Look at the bot card and Activity. The guide says warm-up and recovery states remain visible there.

questions.question: What happens when the Optimized bot cannot load one of its data windows?
questions.answer: It keeps that window’s missing or stale state visible and retries retrieval. It should not treat unavailable history as a valid signal.

questions.question: Can I disable one Optimized pair filter without changing the others?
questions.answer: Yes. Pair filters are independent rules. Change the intended control, save, and review the resulting pair eligibility list.

questions.question: Does Optimized Liquidation calculate a separate TP engine?
questions.answer: It hands accepted deals to the shared deal engine. The configured take-profit and stop-loss controls manage the resulting position.

questions.question: Why does the Optimized worked example use two different pairs?
questions.answer: It demonstrates that one bot configuration can produce different pair-specific behavior because the bands are calculated per market.

questions.question: If I raise the liquidation threshold, will the Optimized bands move?
questions.answer: No. The event threshold determines which liquidation prints count; the bands come from the pair’s recent history and their own settings.

questions.question: Can TradingView call a webhook on a private LAN address?
questions.answer: No. TradingView’s servers need a public, reachable HTTPS address. A private LAN or local address cannot receive the alert.

questions.question: What should I verify before creating a TradingView alert?
questions.answer: Confirm the TV Signal bot is saved, its public HTTPS webhook URL is reachable, the certificate is valid, TradingView webhook notifications are enabled, and the alert uses the bot’s documented message format.

questions.question: Why must I preserve the path at the end of the webhook URL?
questions.answer: That path identifies the specific bot endpoint. If it is changed or copied from another bot, the request will not reach the intended bot.

questions.question: Is the TradingView webhook URL editable after the bot is created?
questions.answer: The URL is read-only and fixed for that bot’s life. The form provides a Copy button for the exact address.

questions.question: Does the TV Signal parser accept arbitrary JSON fields?
questions.answer: Use only the message formats documented in the TV Signal payload guide. Unsupported fields or extra text can make a message malformed or refused.

questions.question: Which TV Signal actions can omit the symbol?
questions.answer: The documented exceptions are close everything, pause, and resume. Other actions need a symbol.

questions.question: What can someone do with my TV Signal URL and secret?
questions.answer: They can send trading actions to that bot, including opening or closing deals and changing or pausing it. Keep the address and secret private; rotate the secret if exposed.

questions.question: Why does the TV Signal form show a different webhook health status from the alert?
questions.answer: The form reports whether the app received the request. If the alert is missing, troubleshoot reachability and TradingView delivery; if it arrived, use the recorded refusal reason.

questions.question: What does an unauthorized TradingView signal usually mean?
questions.answer: The secret did not match or the message was malformed. Re-copy the bot’s documented template and check for smart quotes, extra text, or a template from another bot.

questions.question: Why does a paused TV Signal bot refuse alerts?
questions.answer: Pause is an active refusal state, not a queue. Alerts received while paused are not replayed after you resume.

questions.question: Can the TV Signal bot reject a pair because another bot owns it?
questions.answer: Yes. A pair has one manager at a time. Recent signals reports when another bot owns the pair and prevents the second bot from opening a competing deal.

questions.question: What should I check if my TV Signal alert got a green tick but the wrong coin opened?
questions.answer: Check the actual symbol in the alert payload. The TradingView {{ticker}} placeholder can send the chart’s symbol instead of the exact exchange market symbol expected by the bot.

questions.question: Does a TV Signal message size replace the bot’s saved Base order?
questions.answer: If the message contains its own size, that value overrides Base order for that deal. Inspect the payload and Recent signals before sending another alert.

questions.question: Does the TV Signal bot have a separate DCA implementation?
questions.answer: It uses the shared deal engine and the same DCA ladder behavior described in the common DCA section. Its webhook determines the entry; the ladder manages the deal afterward.

questions.question: Does TV Signal take profit re-anchor when a DCA fills?
questions.answer: Yes. Its take profit is measured from average entry and re-anchors after the average changes from a DCA or manual add.

questions.question: Does Manual Bot change my entry price when it adopts a position?
questions.answer: No. Adoption changes who manages the position; it does not change size, leverage, or average entry on the exchange.

questions.question: Could Manual Bot miss the exchange event that opens a position?
questions.answer: If a private position event is missed, the app’s recovery checks can detect it afterward. The guide describes a fallback adoption path rather than assuming the event was received.

questions.question: Can Manual Bot take over an order that another bot has not confirmed yet?
questions.answer: No. An unresolved order can hold ownership of the pair until its outcome is known. Manual Bot blocks adoption rather than guessing whether a position exists.

questions.question: What happens if both long and short sides of a pair are open but untracked?
questions.answer: The Manual Bot does not adopt either leg while both sides are open and neither is tracked. The guide says to close one side at the venue and review the ownership reason.

questions.question: Does Manual Bot have a Base order or leverage setting?
questions.answer: No. It never opens the initial position, so it has no entry size or leverage control of its own.

questions.question: What does Save & enable do on the Manual Bot form?
questions.answer: It saves the bot configuration and starts the bot if it was not running. Review the saved state in My Bots afterward.

questions.question: If I switch Manual Bot off, are its active take-profit orders removed?
questions.answer: Pausing stops new adoption; it does not mean abandoning managed positions. Existing deals remain managed through their exits.

questions.question: What is the protection difference between Manual Bot TP and SL?
questions.answer: The take profit is an exchange-held reduce-only order. The stop loss is app-managed, so server availability matters for stop monitoring.

questions.question: Can Manual Bot use multiple take-profit targets?
questions.answer: Its exit form supports a take-profit ladder with multiple targets and partial exits. Use the form’s ladder fields to configure the slices.

questions.question: Why does the bot say “not a managed perpetual” for my position?
questions.answer: The position is outside the supported managed futures position type, such as a spot balance or dated future. Manual Bot will not adopt that position.

questions.question: Does Hedge Bot open a position by itself when I enable it?
questions.answer: No. It attaches to eligible positions that already exist. A hedge tranche can open only when price reaches a configured adverse-move level and the required checks pass.

questions.question: What is the difference between Hedge Mode and One-Way mode for hedging?
questions.answer: Hedge Mode holds long and short positions on the same symbol separately. One-Way mode nets them together, so an opposite order can reduce or close the main position instead of hedging it.

questions.question: Can Hedge Bot attach to positions opened by another Wick Hunter bot?
questions.answer: Yes, eligible existing positions can be watched by Hedge Bot, subject to the ownership and attachment rules. The hedge leg itself remains owned by Hedge Bot.

questions.question: Can I exclude one coin from automatic hedge attachment?
questions.answer: Yes. Use the Hedge Bot’s blacklist or pair scope settings to exclude the pair, then save and verify the active scope.

questions.question: How do I make Hedge Bot wait for a certain number of DCAs first?
questions.answer: Enable Minimum DCA to Hedge in Advanced settings and choose the catch-all count or a per-bot count. A value of 0 allows immediate hedging.

questions.question: What does a blank bot row mean in Minimum DCA to Hedge?
questions.answer: A blank per-bot value uses the catch-all minimum. Enter a separate count only when that bot should have a different threshold.

questions.question: Is each hedge ladder Size % the size of the new tranche?
questions.answer: No. It is the total hedge you want held at that level. The actual added amount is based on the target total and the hedge already open.

questions.question: Why can the actual hedge amount be smaller than the level target?
questions.answer: The bot may be constrained by the unstopped size budget, minimum tranche size, venue limits, or current open hedge exposure. Check the active panel for the reason.

questions.question: When is a hedge tranche considered protected?
questions.answer: Only after an actual stop has been armed for it. Before that, even a profitable tranche is counted as unprotected exposure.

questions.question: Does the safe-zone setting count as a hedge stop?
questions.answer: No. Safe zone is an anti-churn pause after a hedge tranche stop-out or paired take profit. It waits for price to move farther against the main before allowing new hedge tranches; it is not itself a stop order.

questions.question: Do per-level Max w/o stop values replace the global hedge budget?
questions.answer: At a configured DCA level, its own unstopped budget replaces the global cap for that level. Review the ladder and global cap together to understand the available size.

questions.question: Does the paired target close the main position if a hedge stop already fired?
questions.answer: The paired target applies to the main position and hedge legs still open. A hedge tranche already closed by its armed stop contributes its realized result to the combined calculation as documented.

questions.question: Does the hedge trail turn itself on by default?
questions.answer: No. The trail switch is off by default. When enabled, it affects only hedge stops that are already armed.

questions.question: Does a new Hedge Bot start with blank fields like the other bots?
questions.answer: Yes. A new Hedge Bot starts with its numeric and name fields blank, like the other new bot forms. Choose the settings before saving; existing bots reopen with their saved values.

questions.question: When does a Hedge Bot use LONG MAIN versus SHORT MAIN settings?
questions.answer: The selected column follows the direction of the main position when the hedge attaches. It is chosen for that attachment and does not change afterward.

questions.question: Can I open the active hedge panel from a deal?
questions.answer: Yes. Use View hedge on the deal to open the panel with that position already selected.

questions.question: Does expanding the hedge chart reset my zoom?
questions.answer: No. The expanded view keeps the chart open with its zoom and hedge lines; restore or Escape returns to the pair panel.

questions.question: Can DCA orders fill during one candle even if price never closes at each level?
questions.answer: Yes. The guide says levels fill when price touches them, so a single candle can cross several levels without a close or bounce at each one.

questions.question: Is the Liq Scalper DCA ladder re-anchored after every fill?
questions.answer: No. The static ladder remains measured from the original opening price; later DCA fills change average entry but do not move the remaining static levels.

questions.question: Why do later DCA orders grow so quickly with Volume scale above 1?
questions.answer: The multiplier applies successively to each order, so each level is based on the previous order’s size. Review the full generated ladder, not only the first step.

questions.question: How can I make DCA orders stay the same size at every level?
questions.answer: Set Volume scale to 1, then verify the generated ladder preview. The guide’s example shows that a scale of 1 keeps each order equal.

questions.question: How can I make DCA gaps grow farther apart at deeper levels?
questions.answer: Use a Step scale above 1. The preview shows the resulting level distances; choose values based on your own risk limits.

questions.question: Why can Scaled ATR refuse an entry instead of using my static deviation?
questions.answer: The guide deliberately refuses an entry when required ATR data is missing, stale, or unsupported. It does not silently substitute a distance you did not choose.

questions.question: What does ATR minimum deviation protect against?
questions.answer: It prevents the first ATR-based DCA distance from falling too close on a quiet pair, where ordinary noise could trigger the level early.

questions.question: What does ATR maximum deviation protect against?
questions.answer: It caps how far away the first ATR-based level can be on a highly volatile pair. With no ceiling, a level can become so distant that it never fills.

questions.question: Can I set ATR maximum lower than ATR minimum?
questions.answer: No. The form refuses a maximum below the minimum because the configured range would be invalid.

questions.question: Does ATR DCA borrow the VWMA timeframe and period?
questions.answer: No. ATR DCA has its own timeframe and length; the VWMA settings are for entry timing, while ATR settings size the ladder.

questions.question: When are ATR-based DCA levels calculated for a deal?
questions.answer: They are calculated once when the deal opens and remain frozen for that deal, even if the pair becomes more volatile later.

questions.question: Does a percent base order keep scaling with balance after the deal opens?
questions.answer: No. It converts the percentage to a dollar amount once at deal opening and keeps that amount fixed for the deal’s life.

questions.question: Can the Summary panel cap the total position if the calculated exposure is high?
questions.answer: No. It is a preview of the math, not a trading limit. Reduce the base order or ladder settings yourself if total exposure is too high.

questions.question: Does Manual Bot re-plan its DCA ladder after I add to the position?
questions.answer: The guide says the ladder is worked out from the position as it stood at pickup and is not re-planned afterward. Check the current deal values before changing it manually.

questions.question: Why do all unfilled DCAs need replacement when I edit the ladder?
questions.answer: Each resting DCA price depends on the ladder. Since the exchange cannot edit those orders in place, the app cancels and replaces the affected resting orders after commit.

questions.question: Can I move only DCA 3 without changing DCA 2?
questions.answer: You can drag DCA 3’s own handle, but the staged ladder may require cancelling and re-placing other unfilled DCAs because their prices are calculated from the ladder. Review the staged bar before commit.

questions.question: Does the fixed take profit follow the highest price after entry?
questions.answer: No. Fixed % rests a target and does not follow favorable price changes. Trailing is the mode that follows price after activation.

questions.question: Does a partial Manual Bot take-profit close change the deal’s average entry?
questions.answer: No. A partial close books that slice and removes its share of cost basis; it does not move the remaining position’s average entry.

questions.question: Can I configure ATR take profit and multiple TP targets together?
questions.answer: The guide lists ATR as a single-target source. Check the current exit form for which modes can be combined; do not assume settings from different modes apply together.

questions.question: What does a trailing take-profit activation value control?
questions.answer: It controls when the trailing target begins following favorable movement. The offset then determines its distance from the favorable price reached.

questions.question: What does “stop loss off” leave in place?
questions.answer: With the stop-loss switch off, Wick Hunter has no configured stop-loss close for that deal. Take profit and any separately enabled hedge behavior remain governed by their own settings.

questions.question: Does a stop-loss percent always mean percent below the first entry?
questions.answer: No. Its meaning depends on the selected offset basis. Read the field’s basis and example before deciding what price the percentage produces.

questions.question: Why does the stop-loss guide distinguish an exchange order from a monitor?
questions.answer: An exchange-held stop can remain at the venue if the app is unavailable; an app monitor needs Wick Hunter running to detect the trigger and send a close. Check the venue-specific behavior for your deal.

questions.question: Can the Manual Bot’s app-managed stop work while the server is down?
questions.answer: No. An app-managed stop needs the server to monitor price and submit the exit. The Manual Bot take-profit order is held at the exchange, which is a separate control.

questions.question: What does hedge trailing change after a stop is armed?
questions.answer: It moves the armed stop toward the price as the hedge tranche earns, potentially locking more of the move. It does not trail the main position or arm an unprotected tranche.

questions.question: Does Bybit’s Full / TP Entire price equal the paired target on the deal?
questions.answer: No. Full / TP Entire is a separate conditional target for the main position; the paired target is a projected combined result watched by Wick Hunter. While the hedge owns the exit, the app removes that main-position target and restores its recipe when the hedge closes.

questions.question: Why can the paired TP price be described as projected?
questions.answer: It represents the price where the combined main-plus-hedge result would reach its target under the app’s calculation. It is watched by Wick Hunter, not resting at the venue.

questions.question: Why is today’s P&L day different from my local midnight?
questions.answer: Wick Hunter groups P&L by UTC day, not by the browser’s local timezone. Compare it to the UTC date shown by the app and exchange.

questions.question: Does the P&L page guess a missing exchange fee?
questions.answer: No. If the venue does not provide enough information to assign a fee to a trade, the page shows less data rather than guessing.

questions.question: Why does my wallet balance not equal total closed P&L?
questions.answer: Wallet balance can reflect deposits, withdrawals, open-position changes, funding, and exchange-specific reporting differences. The P&L page reports the history the venue exposes; compare the same basis and time range.

questions.question: Can I export the wallet or equity chart data?
questions.answer: Yes. Use the CSV control to export the currently selected series. Missing wallet samples remain empty rather than being filled with guessed values.

questions.question: Does a dotted Terminal order line mean the order is already resting on the exchange?
questions.answer: No. It is a planned limit price; nothing rests on the exchange until you send the order and the venue accepts it.

questions.question: How do I know how far the WEEX history import has progressed?
questions.answer: The history note reports how far the import has reached. The import stores progress, retries unavailable reads, and keeps older downloaded records locally.

questions.question: Does reaching the full WEEX API history window prove there are no older trades?
questions.answer: No. Completing the available API window does not prove the account has no history beyond what WEEX made available.

questions.question: Does Terminal show the open deal on its own exchange candles?
questions.answer: Yes. It draws one selected open deal on candles from the exchange and product for that deal, with its relevant order levels marked.

questions.question: What does the Avg Price tag refer to?
questions.answer: It marks the position’s blended average entry. It is not an order and cannot be dragged.

questions.question: Why do order lines have labels beside them and numbers on the right axis?
questions.answer: The labels identify each order line, while the numeric right axis stays clear and readable when several lines are present.

questions.question: Will Escape cancel a staged order edit?
questions.answer: Yes. Escape abandons the staged drag without contacting the server and returns the line to the price currently held by the exchange.

questions.question: Can a red chart line still be committed?
questions.answer: A red handle warns that the staged value is invalid for the order. Review & commit remains disabled while a change is refused; adjust it to an allowed price first.

questions.question: What happens if a resting order cannot be changed in place?
questions.answer: The app confirms cancellation, then places a replacement order. The staged bar previews the cancels and placements before you commit.

questions.question: Does a committed Terminal edit change the bot’s future settings?
questions.answer: No. A committed edit belongs only to that deal and persists with that deal; it does not change the bot template.

questions.question: What can I use the Terminal order ticket for?
questions.answer: It is the app’s manual-order entry point. When enabled, you select buy or sell, market or limit, and a size; it is separate from bot signal execution.

questions.question: Can I set order size as a percent of balance in the Terminal ticket?
questions.answer: The ticket supports sizing in dollars, contracts, or a percentage of balance. Review the displayed order details before submitting the manual order.

questions.question: Does clicking a paired TP line place an order?
questions.answer: No. The paired TP is a watched combined target. Use Review & commit for supported manual line edits; the paired target itself is not a venue limit order.

questions.question: Which candles does Wick Hunter use for a Bybit USDT perpetual?
questions.answer: It uses Bybit’s linear book for USDT perpetuals. Spot and inverse contracts use their own corresponding books.

questions.question: Which candles does a spot strategy use?
questions.answer: It uses the exchange’s Spot book, not the futures book.

questions.question: Can liquidation events come from a different venue than the traded pair?
questions.answer: A selected liquidation feed may contribute the event, but the bot evaluates the corresponding symbol on its own trading venue and uses that venue’s candles.

questions.question: Does the chart export include both Wallet and Equity when I selected one?
questions.answer: The CSV exports the series currently selected. Choose Equity or Wallet balance first if you want to export the other view.

questions.question: Can I view Daily candles in the hedge chart?
questions.answer: Yes. Choose Daily in the chart timeframe row. Changing timeframe keeps the selected chart’s zoom and hedge context.

questions.question: Why is the latest point missing from wallet history?
questions.answer: A missing wallet reading remains empty in the chart or CSV. Wick Hunter does not invent a wallet sample it did not receive.

questions.question: Can a pair have two Wick Hunter bots managing it at once?
questions.answer: No. A pair has one manager at a time so bot ownership stays unambiguous. Check the Deals and Activity views to see which bot owns a position.

questions.question: Why can Aster closed P&L differ slightly from the wallet?
